summary.headline: Moneyboxx Q4 FY26 total income rose to INR63.23 crore (from INR52 crore), but Q4 PAT was only INR0.47 crore amid high credit costs and AUM at INR893 crore.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of transition, correction and strengthening, after MFI guardrails and stress in small-ticket secured lending hit collections and asset quality. Secured loans rose to about 68% of AUM (from 45% a year earlier), and collection efficiency was around 93.5% for the quarter. Gross NPA was 3.59% and net NPA 1.75%, both lower year on year, but Q4 profit was thin and AUM was down versus last year due to an ARC transaction. Management guided to AUM growth of 43-44% for FY27 and a sharp pickup in disbursements from May 2026, while acknowledging moderate growth so far.

financial_highlights.change: 6% growth as stated; management said YoY decline was due to ARC transaction
vs INR52 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Secured lending (MSME, branch-led)
segments.commentary: Secured share of AUM about 68% (5% of this is unsecured backed by first-loss fee guarantee), up from 45% last year. Secured disbursements were 67% versus 49% last year; target is nearly 80% secured AUM by March 2027. Average secured ticket size is INR6 lakh, with run-rate INR8-9 lakh.

segments.name: Renewable energy (solar) loans
segments.commentary: Launched in FY26; disbursements were about INR50 lakh in April, ramping roughly 10x in May to a possible INR5 crore. Management targets about 10% of AUM by March 2027. Average ticket about INR4 lakh, tenure about 4 years, yield about 22-24% including fees, with a second-loss fee guarantee after 3% first loss.

segments.name: Unsecured / digital lending
segments.commentary: Unsecured lending to be restricted to one state; below INR5 lakh secured ticket discontinued in most branches from April. A small digital unsecured lending initiative is planned to start in the current quarter, enabled by the in-house LOS Moneyboxx One.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth of 43-44% projected, as communicated to lenders; management said it has historically met lender-committed numbers.
Credit cost expected to fall below 2% in FY27, from 3.32% in FY26.
Disbursements expected to be better than last year in Q1 FY27 and far better in Q2 FY27; month-on-month growth expected from May-June 2026.
Direct OEM/partner-sourced business targeted at 20-25% of monthly business to lower opex; two more partnerships starting in June 2026.
Net worth considered adequate for FY27 plan; co-lending partnerships in secured space to be pursued; equity raise targeted in second half of FY27.
No new geographies in FY26-27; branch network to decline on a net basis via consolidation of rural branches and openings in Tier 1 cities.
capex_capacity: Branch network across 12 states; management is not seeking to expand branch count, consolidating rural branches and opening a few in Tier 1 areas (2 in Bangalore periphery, 1 in Jaipur).
Many branches are in early vintage (under 24 months); productivity is expected to improve as they mature, supporting operating leverage without aggressive expansion.
Newly launched in-house LOS Moneyboxx One and Sikka app are expected to improve turnaround time and field productivity, with benefits in coming months.
Decentralised credit underwriting model deployed, replacing the earlier centralised credit model.
demand_pricing: Management attributed slower growth to tighter underwriting after MFI stress, a state-head team rebuild and the shift to higher-ticket secured loans; some decline in demand acknowledged, with lenders across the sector tightening norms.
Secured yields will be lower; partnership and FLDG-backed business is expected to offset through lower opex and credit cost, per management.
Resolution rates improved: bucket 1 above 70% and bucket 2 above 75%, versus about 30-35% earlier. Current-bucket efficiency rose to over 99.4% in March from about 99% in January.
Management sees collection stress concentrated in the INR3-4 lakh secured ticket segment; SARFAESI and Section 138 actions started from May 2026.
Management expects a seasonal April-June weakness to be offset by solar loans, which peak in those months.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AUM growth remained moderate despite better collections and disbursements, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the post-MFI-guardrail shift, a senior team overhaul, decentralised credit and removal of sub-INR5 lakh secured tickets. It said top leadership is now in place, and that disbursements and AUM should grow month-on-month from May-June 2026, with FY27 AUM growth of 43-44% projected.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost appears high relative to AUM; how will opex come down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged high cost, attributing it to low AUM and hiring experienced staff; said cost should fall as AUM grows and that 20-25% of monthly business will come through partnerships without a sales team.

qa_highlights.question: Will the shift to secured lending lower yields, and what are the ROA/ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management accepted that yields will fall on secured and partnership business, but said lower opex and credit cost should offset this. It cited peers at 12-15% returns on assets as the benchmark, without giving specific ROA/ROE targets.

qa_highlights.question: Any new geographies or products planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No new states in FY27; the 12-state footprint is considered sufficient. Solar is the new product (about 10% of AUM targeted), with one or two more products and a cattle-loan FLDG partnership planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand slowing due to macro uncertainty and inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said appetite exists, but lenders have tightened norms and some demand has declined. Lending to restaurants was paused due to LPG shortage. It pointed to green shoots in the MFI segment and government guarantee support for working-capital loans.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the QoQ rise in GNPA and what is the Q1 FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Stress was concentrated in INR3-4 lakh secured loans and an older stressed book. Management said GNPA is falling monthly since January, with SARFAESI from May; disbursements in Q1 FY27 should beat last year, and Q2 should be far better.

risks_watch: Growth delivery: FY27 AUM growth of 43-44% and the month-on-month disbursement recovery must be shown in upcoming quarters, given two years of slow growth.
Credit cost must fall from 3.32% to below 2%, while the older stressed portfolio is worked through legal recovery and SARFAESI.
Opex is high relative to AUM (employee cost about 37-38% of AUM per an analyst, not disputed by management); yield dilution from secured shift could compress NIM from 13.9%.
Equity raise targeted in H2 FY27 depends on market conditions; management referenced the ongoing war as affecting markets.
Agricultural and rural cash flow risk: management flagged fertiliser supply, rainfall and food grain inflation as risks for next year's repayments.
Digital unsecured lending launch and two new OEM partnerships in June 2026 are unproven at scale.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the past year, acknowledging moderate growth, high opex and a thin Q4 profit. Confident on forward recovery, but most forward claims (AUM growth, disbursement pickup, GNPA decline) are not yet backed by reported data.
key_quotes: So, although you're getting a lower yield a bit, but on the cost side and on the credit cost side, we save money.
I think last 2 years have been on a high credit cost side. This year, we seriously expect that this number should go down below 2%.
Overall, FY '26 was a year of transition, correction and strengthening of the company.

adds.what: Branch openings in Tier 1 areas (2 in Bangalore periphery, 1 in Jaipur) offset by rural branch consolidation; net branch count to decline

growth.why: Management guided FY27 AUM growth of 43-44% and credit cost below 2%, backed by solar loans (~10% of AUM by Mar 2027), a secured mix shift and partner/OEM sourcing, but no specific capacity or contracted orders quantify the AUM jump and the brief notes some demand decline and a thin Q4 PAT of INR0.47 crore.
